root_idea.summary: The root centers on an opening, cleft, hollow, or separation in something, especially in the structure of the back; its semantic field extends from hollows and vertebrae to breaking, affliction, and need.
root_idea.development: The vertebrae are understood as separated segments of the back, while poverty is conventionally explained as a condition resembling a broken back or lacking support. This development also underlies terms for calamity, hollows, and making something accessible through an opening.

senses.definition: A calamity or misfortune that breaks the back.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative noun for a grievous affliction; Quranic usage occurs in the description of an impending severe calamity.

senses.definition: In need of, dependent upon, or lacking self-sufficiency.
senses.usage_conditions: This includes essential dependence, especially dependence upon God; with إِلَى, the object is what or whom one needs or requires.

senses.definition: Poor or needy in material means, lacking sufficient property, livelihood, or resources.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of individuals or groups who lack adequate means; the Quranic usage includes the poor as recipients or objects of charitable provision. Classical discussions differ over the precise distinction between فَقِير and مِسْكِين.

senses.definition: Poverty, material want, or lack of sufficient possessions.
senses.usage_conditions: A state of material need, presented in the Quranic context as the opposite of wealth and as a condition from which people may fear being deprived of means.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig into the ground or dig a well in order to bring out water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the action is understood as making a hollow or opening in the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bore or perforate beads so that they may be strung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; used specifically of piercing beads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave, slit, or rend something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; a physical opening or splitting apart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incise the muzzle of a refractory camel down to, or nearly to, the bone, and attach a controlling cord there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; a specialized camel-training procedure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stigmatize a person by exposing or recounting his faults.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributed figurative use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break the vertebrae of someone's back; figuratively, for a calamity to befall someone as though breaking the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I transitive and figurative uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a complaint of the vertebrae arising from fracture or disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I usage describing a vertebral ailment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig a hollow for a palm shoot or offset when planting it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II verb; the hollow is prepared to receive the young palm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incise, notch, impress, or mark something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II passive and related uses describe a surface bearing such cuts or impressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strong in the vertebrae and fit to be ridden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV, said of a colt or its back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lend someone the back or vertebrae of a camel, colt, or other mount for riding or carrying a burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV construction with the animal or its back as the object; the mount is lent for a journey and returned afterward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lend someone land for sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form IV extension from lending the back of a mount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For game to become accessible to a shooter, especially by bringing its side or back within reach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression أَفْقَرَكَ الصَّيْدُ means that the object of the chase has become available to you to shoot; it can also mean that it has come near.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone poor or needy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To elicit what is hidden or obscure in knowledge and bring it to light.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form V reading in a transmitted expression; the commonly known reading is a different verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign the lowliness or submissiveness associated with poverty and humble oneself among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI reciprocal or affective use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave, slit, or rend open; figuratively, to open and make obscure meanings clear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII; the figurative use describes unveiling or clarifying what was concealed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become poor or needy, or to need or require someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII; with إِلَى, it means to need or require the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To borrow or request the loan of a camel's back for riding or carrying a burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form X specialized construction with a mount as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anxiety, mental disquietude, or one's circumstances and pressing wants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader nominal use distinct from simple material poverty; the plural may refer to a person's anxieties or troubles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side of the body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal use, with an irregular plural noted in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal usage; the lexical evidence also discusses its collective or plural form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow dug in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical depression or excavation; plural فُقَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An incision made in a camel's muzzle; figuratively, a grievous or formidable event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative sense develops from the series of incisions used to control a refractory camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part of a shirt through which the head is inserted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal term for the garment opening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearness or proximity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression هُوَ مِنِّي فُقْرَةً, meaning that someone is near to the speaker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An ornament fashioned in the form of a vertebra.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural term for such ornaments; the sense is based on resemblance to the vertebrae of the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A choice or salient unit of poetic or rhymed discourse, including the best verse of an ode, a choice phrase, or a clause ending in rhyme.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative literary use extended from the idea of a vertebral segment or prominent part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of land suitable for sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal agricultural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark or landmark used by people competing in shooting or casting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to a mountain, hill, hollow, or other target-like landmark used to specify a shooting position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lending of a camel or other mount to be ridden or used for carrying a burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive derived from the Form IV construction أَفْقَرَهُ نَاقَتَهُ or أَفْقَرَهُ بَعِيرَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vertebrae of the back or the bones of the spine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective or singular lexical term for the regularly arranged spinal bones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The three bright stars arranged obliquely in the middle of Orion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative astronomical designation based on the appearance of vertebrae in a row.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a celebrated sword associated first with the Prophet and later with ʿAlī.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name explained as referring to hollows or indentations in the sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spear, by metaphorical extension from the name of the sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative weapon term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow or well, especially one made around a palm shoot, and by extension a series of wells or a place where wells are dug.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the adjective meaning poor; the well may be old, shallow, or one of several communicating wells.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mouth or outlet from which water issues from a subterranean channel or conduit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized geographical or hydraulic noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollowed palm trunk used to ascend to an upper chamber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical use; the evidence notes that نَقِير is the more commonly known word in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having an incision made in the muzzle, said of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet describing the camel-training procedure associated with فَقَرَ أَنْفَ البَعِيرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with broken or diseased vertebrae, or struck by a calamity as though the back had been broken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to a person; this is a physical or figurative affliction, not the ordinary poverty sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person disabled or weakened by illness, especially prolonged disease that prevents earning adequately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized classical description of a materially vulnerable person, distinguished in some accounts from other kinds of need.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The resurrection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative nominal use reported as an extension of the calamity sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong in the vertebrae or back and fit to be ridden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, camel, or colt; of a colt, it can mean having reached riding age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm-minded, strong, or capable enough for an undertaking or opponent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on strength of the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword whose blade has notches or indentations forming depressions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective describing the blade's shaped surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Containing many hollows or depressions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to land containing numerous فُقَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who claims to be in poverty or need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description of professed or asserted poverty.

cautions: The classical distinction between فَقِير and مِسْكِين is disputed; the Quranic فقير forms are therefore defined by attested need and insufficient means without imposing one disputed ranking.
The Form V sense تَفَقَّرَ is preserved as a reported reading because the same evidence states that the commonly known reading is تَقَفَّرَ.
The palm-trunk sense of فَقِير is reported with an explicit qualification that نَقِير is the more commonly known term in that usage.
